newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia reserves $23.8 bln July 1 ($20 bln June 23).
newsitem.headline: Russia reserves $23.8 bln July 1 ($20 bln June 23).

text.p: Russia's gross gold and currency reserves rose to $23.8 billion on July 1, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin told a news conference on Wednesday.
Reserves had totaled $20 billion, including $2.5 billion in gold, on June 23 and about $19 billion on June 5, he had said earlier. He gave no separate figures for gold reserves on Wednesday.
Dubinin said the Central Bank, which has actively been buying dollars on the foreign exchange market as investors purchase roubles and T-bills, was effectively issuing roubles.
There had been a considerable increase in hard currency/gold reserves, but growth would probably slow in the second half of the year due to seasonal dollar sales, he said.
He said M2 money supply, which includes savings accounts and cash in circulation, rose by 24 percent in the first half of the year.

"The main source of (M2) growth is a rise in cash volume by about 34 percent," he said. "The cash portion of M2 rose from 35 percent to 38 percent. This is based on rising demand for roubles under expectations of falling inflation."

Dubinin told the State Duma lower parliament house in March there was a 15 percent quota on foreign participation in the government securities market, although it was not clear if he meant a quota for primary issues or for secondary market holdings.
Deputy Chairman Alexander Potyomkin told Reuters on Wednesday foreigners held about 30 percent of all paper issued.
Dubinin also said the bank also was not planning to lower its refinancing rate, which is effectively a cap on T-bill yields.

"We do not think it is expedient to change our refinancing rates," Dubinin said. On June 16, the bank lowered the key rate to 24 percent from 36 percent. T-bill yields are now testing levels around 20 percent. The bank wants to avoid the risks of foreigners pulling out of the market quickly.
